commitment_rule.granularity: one commitment, with its own independent salt, per committed value

precision.note: Encoding is an exact multiplication. A value not exactly representable at this precision is an error, never a rounded value: section 3.3.1 requires the tooling to reject rather than quietly prove a quantized value the client never intended. The precision itself is provisional per section 10.1, pending methodology-owner sign-off.

rounding.note: This is the rounding of the product back down to the pinned precision, inside the circuit. It is a separate decision from the encoding above, which does not round at all.

next.with: the proof, its proof_sha256, the public_signals array and the formula id and version, all from the package prove returned
next.note: Copy the proof exactly as the prover gave it, and always send proof_sha256 with it: the two are checked against each other here, and ~19KB of base64 is long enough that a message can truncate or reflow it. If that check refuses, call verify again with include_proof: true to read a clean copy off disk, and send that. A prover configured with its own API key can post the package itself instead, which avoids the copy entirely.
